title: MOXIR 17.10 — three versions of the rig: minimal, middle, full
status: PROPOSAL for the owner's look. Same hall, same DJ booth, same zones as the base rig; what changes is how much is hung and how it is used. Nothing here is checked against the venue, a load calculation or the rental house.
owner: 2026-09-28, on /moxir: "make 3 version with the full, midle, and simple minimalistic and also look to moxir mood, set, vibe and its the undegroudn rave thing lights like that not the commercial shit"

method.what: Each version is a complete rig file generated from the base (scripts/place/rigs/moxir-2026-10-17.json) by scripts/rigbuild/versions.mjs: the base's stage, truss, night, photometry and opening, this file's groups, effects, budget and looks. The three files are committed beside the base and checked current by a test.
method.practice: The underground rules below are the design brief. Where a source was opened and says it, it is cited (sources); where no citable source was found in this session they are marked 'design hypothesis' — scene practice widely repeated but not documented by a source we could open (web search budget exhausted 2026-09-28; owed: RA In Residence: Bassiani 2017-02-01, RA 'Tbilisi and the politics of raving' 2016-08-15, Vice 'Is This Georgian Club the New Berghain?' 2017-06-16 — confirmed to exist, not read).

rules.rule: Darkness is a material: most of the room is unlit most of the time; a look says where light is NOT (levels 0).
The building is the set: its structure revealed in pieces (a column, the press, the roof frame), never floodlit or decorated.
Strobes are the peak: violent white hits against the industrial fabric, then dark again.
Heavy haze, so a beam reads as a column of the architecture rather than a spot on the floor.
One colour at a time, and few of them: cold white, deep red, a warm amber (the blinders' tungsten-like white); never rainbow chases.
Light from low and from behind: the DJ in silhouette, not in a key light.
Stillness and slow sweeps, then a hit: the looks are held states, the movement is between them.
None of the commercial vocabulary: no CO2 jets, cold sparks, confetti or butterfly effects.
rules.status: design hypothesis — the owner's own words ('not the commercial shit') are the brief

ATMOSFERA.what: Pietro Leonardi, 'The role of light design in Nightclubs', Atmosfera Mag (undated; opened 2026-09-28): "The Berghain floor remains mostly dark, mirroring the intense and relentless techno played within"; on warehouse raves, "strobe lights creating intense visual contrasts against the industrial backdrops"

MIXMAG-2018.what: Duncan Dick, 'The art of club design', Mixmag, 31 Aug 2018 (opened 2026-09-28). Simeon Aldred (Printworks London): "The key to a 'found' space is not to change it drastically, but to amplify what is already there." "Make it safe for the audience, but then leave it alone."

DAZED-2016.what: Dazed, 'Lightning strikes Berghain but party rages on', 30-31 Aug 2016 (opened by the research agent 2026-09-28): the emergency lights coming on described as 'blinding bright' — bright light as the exception

WIKI-BERGHAIN.what: Wikipedia, 'Berghain' (opened 2026-09-28): "a cavernous main room with 18-meter ceilings and is dominated by steel and concrete"; no photographs inside

WIKI-BASSIANI.what: Wikipedia, 'Bassiani' (opened 2026-09-28): "utilizes a disused swimming pool as the main dance floor" in the Dinamo Arena; photography banned

WIKI-TRESOR.what: Wikipedia, 'Tresor (club)' (opened by the research agent 2026-09-28): the vaults of a former department store, since 2007 the decommissioned Heizkraftwerk Berlin-Mitte

IEC-60825-1.what: IEC 60825-1, safety of laser products — the MPE limits a laser safety officer works to (named, not applied here)

palette.why: One colour at a time, and few of them (rule 5). Every look colour must be one of these; a test holds it.

hazer-hall.label: hazer
hazer-hall.note: hazers along the nave columns, so the far half of the hall holds haze too

white-cathedral.title: White cathedral
white-cathedral.intent: The roof frame and the columns as a nave of cold white: the column beams stand straight up in mirrored pairs, the booth's line opens a narrow apse fan behind the DJ. Everything else is dark — no PAR, no spot, no strobe.

red-room.title: Red room
red-room.intent: Deep red only, and low: the columns and the press glow from their feet, the booth's beams stand still and dim in red, the DJ a dark shape against the red press. The column beams are out: the roof stays black.

strobe-hit.title: Strobe hit
strobe-hit.intent: The peak: every strobe and blinder at full — the pit strobes rake up over the crowd from the floor, the header strobes and the blinders hit the front of the floor; every beam and PAR out, so the flash lands on black.

one-beam.title: Blackout + one beam
one-beam.intent: Everything out but one: the beam on the floor right behind the DJ, straight up into the roof — the DJ a silhouette cut out of it.

slow-sweep.title: Slow sweep
slow-sweep.intent: A held frame of a slow mirrored sweep: the column beams lean out toward the walls in pairs, the booth's line fans wide; the columns glow a low red underneath. Nothing flashes.

versions.title: Minimal — one line under the crane, one colour
versions.summary: No stage, no towers: the DJ stand alone, the crane parked over it. One 8 m line hung from the bridge on 2 chain hoists carries 7 beams standing on it and 2 strobes under it, with 4 red PARs grazing the bridge; 6 column-base beams into the roof, 11 PARs red on the columns and the press, 4 strobes in the pit, 2 hazers.

versions.title: Full — the whole list, used darkly

photometry.why: Heavy haze (rule 4; 2-6 hazers in every version where the base had 4 smoke machines): every cone's air brightness at 1.5 where the base rig draws 0.9. A drawing choice, not photometry — the ratios between the fixtures stay the datasheets'.

The minimal hang, approved: ONE line ("ok take complimentary"). The crane is moved in the hall's dims (moxir-hall-crane-dj-2026-09-28.json: bridge centre over the DJ, z 4.8 m; trolley parked at the right end), not duplicated.

variants.compare: the owner compares it with option 4 ("the cut") on Minimal; a separate project, never Minimal itself
variants.title: Minimal · halo
variants.summary: Simple: NO moving heads, the rental house's fixed lights only (UP-PL5403 PARs, UP-COB200 COB PARs). Minimal's hall; a flat triangle of 3 x 4 m truss at 6 m under the crane bridge over the DJ, apex to the crowd, 3 hoists on bridles. 8 PARs round it focused IN to a ring round the DJ (the cone), the apex PAR straight down (the pillar), the base corners' PARs crossing over the DJ (the X), 4 PARs out to the crowd, 4 red PARs grazing the bridge, 4 COBs on it and 4 in the pit for the hits; the columns and the press in red.
variants.source: owner's option 6 of ~/Downloads/moxir-crane-rig/ten-truss.html ('Halo: a triangle of 3 x 4 m lying flat at 6 m, centred over the DJ; beams on the corners all aim in to a point on the DJ: a cone of light around them, then open outward to the crowd; 3 hoists'), asked 2026-09-29

haloTruss.why: Option 6 of the ten truss versions, built as a comparison beside option 4 on Minimal. The triangle is the object; the lamps live on it.
haloTruss.section_class: 290 mm square box truss (Global Truss F34; Prolyte H30V is the same class)
haloTruss.corner: Global Truss F34 C20 2-way corner 60° (F34C20: 8.80 kg, outer 1000 x 1000 x 290 mm)
haloTruss.corner_source: https://globaltruss.de/en/F34-2-way-corner-C20-600/F34C20 (opened 2026-09-29): "F34 2-way corner C20 60° … Weight: 8,80 kg … Dimensions (L/W/H): 1000 x 1000 x 290 mm". A 60° corner is a STANDARD catalogue part of the 290 mm system (the same series lists C19 45°, C21 90°, C22 120°, C23 135°).
haloTruss.corner_leg_why: The page gives the C20's outer box, not its leg on the centre line. 0.5 m is ASSUMED so a side = 0.5 + 3 m F34300 + 0.5 = 4.0 m node to node; read the real leg from Global Truss's 'DWG files (F34 System)' on the same page before ordering (a longer leg makes the side longer — stock straights only).
haloTruss.orientation: Apex toward the crowd (+z), base edge behind the DJ under the bridge's back girder.
haloTruss.orientation_why: (1) The base edge lies behind the DJ and 0.3 m clear of the press in plan (its truss z 3.50-3.79; the press ends at z 3.2), so nothing hangs over the machine; with the apex toward the press, the triangle's point would sit 0.25 m off the press's left edge and a side would cross over its corner. (2) From the floor the apex points at the people and the two long sides run back to frame the DJ against the press — the halo reads as an arrowhead opening onto the performer. (3) Either way one corner lies beyond the bridge (the triangle is 3.46 m deep, the two girders span 2.9 m face to face); the apex is one pick, the base would be two.

plan_m.note: hall frame, from stageFrame + haloGeometry (the centroid on the bridge centre line z 4.8; the DJ box is z 4.3-6.0)

height_check.stack_m: girder bottom 8.15 - bridle 0.75 (ring) - hoist suspension + body + hook tackle ≈ 0.10 + 0.34 + 0.23 = 0.67 → hook at ≈ 6.73 m (apex, under the outrigger: ≈ 6.44 m); top chord 6.29 m → 0.15-0.44 m of chain and sling left.
height_check.headroom_basis: ChainMaster D8Plus 500 kg (SK030/76U) data sheet DS_CH_D8PLUS_SK_030-76U_500kg_4m_1f-400V-50Hz_DC.pdf, dimension sheet §3 (body 127+131+79 mm, hook tackle 227 mm, suspension plate 97 mm) — the sum is DERIVED from the drawing, the maker publishes no single 'headroom' figure for this build.
height_check.low_rail: At the rail's LOW bound (6.6 m → girder bottom ≈ 7.15 m) the hook is at ≈ 5.73 m and a 6.0 m bottom chord is NOT reachable: the halo then trims at ≈ 5.3 m (bottom chord), still 0.3 m clear of the press crown in plan terms (it is not over the press). Measure the rail.
height_check.press: Nothing hangs over the press in plan (x 0.25-3.05, z 0.2-3.2, crown 5.6 m): the nearest steel is the base edge at z ≥ 3.50 and the right base corner's lamp body at z ≥ 3.49.

rigging.hoist: chain hoist 500 kg, BGV-D8+ (e.g. ChainMaster D8Plus 500 kg SK030/76U; CM Lodestar class)
rigging.hoist_source: ChainMaster D8Plus 500 kg data sheet: 'Weight (without chain): approx. 20 kg', chain 0.59 kg/m (P5.4 x 15)
rigging.per_point: Each corner: a two-leg bridle (a V, legs ±0.75 m, 0.75 m deep: 90° between the legs, each leg ≈ 0.71 x the pick) on beam clamps, a chain hoist hook-suspended under its ring, the chain and a round sling round the corner block; a safety steel from the corner to the crane, independent of the hoist. Base corners: the V along the back girder (it holds x). Apex: the V along the outrigger (it holds z). Three V's in two directions hold the halo in x, z and in turn.
rigging.crane: the nave's entry-end bridge crane, rolled along its runway to park over the DJ; rail height 7.6 m (disputed 6.6-8.4), girder bottom 8.15 m, two 0.7 m box girders at ±1.1 m
rigging.signoff: rigging sign-off owed (crane rated load, lock-out, hoists + safety steels): the crane's rated load and a check of the old runway, rails and brakes; the crane locked in place and its power isolated for the whole event; the apex OUTRIGGER is a cantilever off the bridge (its back clamps are pulled up) and needs a structural engineer's check or a different pick (a bridle to the roof steel, or a 3 m halo that fits under the bridge); a rigger's plan with the point loads, signed by a structural or rigging engineer. This file draws it; they approve it.

sway.concern: Owner, 2026-09-29: moving heads may swing a chain-hung truss.
sway.method: A chain-hung load is a pendulum, T = 2π√(L/g), L = pivot to the load's centre of mass. Out of a bridle's plane the pivot is the girder; in its plane the V is triangulated (stiff). The three V's lie in two directions (x at the base, z at the apex), so the halo is held in x, z and turn; the pendulum below is the bound if a bridle is left out.

rule.text: No head moves full range faster than 4 s (every cue that moves a halo head fades ≥ 4 s; a strobe hit moves nothing); no periodic movement (a chase, a sweep FX) with a period between 1.5 and 6 s — half to twice the pendulum's period — on the halo's heads; heads reposition in black.

sway.tie_offs: Not drawn: with the three bridles none is needed on paper. If the rigger wants more, tie the base corners back to the crane girders with horizontal ratchet straps — never to the crowd floor.
sway.fixed: This version has NO moving heads: nothing on the halo moves, so no head's reaction can set it swinging (the pendulum numbers stay for the heads version).

par-halo-x.note: the two base-corner PARs, focused through one point 3.1 m over the deck above the DJ: they cross in an X on him and run on down past him

par-halo-ring.note: 8 PARs under the two long sides (a fifth of a side apart), each focused IN to a ring 1.3 m round the DJ at deck height: the cone of light round the performer

par-halo-out.note: 4 PARs under the base edge behind the DJ, focused OUT over his head to the crowd, dipped 20°: the halo opening outward

cob-halo.note: 4 COBs hung on the halo (both sides at the middle, the base centre, the apex) facing the crowd for the hits (strobe 1-25 Hz on the desk)

cob-pit.note: 4 COBs on the floor in the pit (x ±1, ±3), raking up over the crowd — the hits from below (where Minimal had strobes; the rental house has none)

par-bridge-back.note: 2 PARs standing on the base edge's top chord, grazing the underside of the BACK girder (over them) outward in deep red

par-bridge-front.note: 2 PARs standing on the sides' top chord (x ±0.6, z 6.07), grazing the underside of the audience-side girder outward in deep red

halo-one-beam.title: Blackout + one beam
halo-one-beam.intent: Everything out but one: the apex PAR straight down — a white pillar in the pit between the crowd and the DJ, who stands behind it as a shape.

halo-slow-sweep.title: Slow sweep
halo-slow-sweep.intent: Fixed lights cannot sweep: the halo OPENS instead — the 4 PARs behind the DJ throw out over his head to the crowd in cold white, the columns and the bridge glow low red. On the desk this is a slow chase across the four (never a move: nothing moves).

halo-red-room.title: Red room
halo-red-room.intent: Deep red and low: the cone's 8 PARs at half in red make a red cage round the DJ, the two base-corner PARs cross in a red X over his head, the columns, the press and the bridge glow red from below; the roof stays black.

halo-white-cathedral.title: White cathedral
halo-white-cathedral.intent: The cone on the DJ: the 8 PARs round the halo at full cold white close in to a ring round him — a cone of light with the performer inside it, the pillar in front; everything else dark.

halo-strobe-hit.title: Strobe hit
halo-strobe-hit.intent: The peak: the 8 COBs (4 on the halo, 4 in the pit) at full in their strobe mode, every PAR out, so the hit lands on black.

show.why: Minimal's five cues, fades and holds (one 60 s pass). Fixed lights: nothing moves, so the sway rule is met by construction; only levels and colours change.

height_check.low_rail: At the rail's LOW bound (6.6 m → girder bottom ≈ 7.15 m) the hook is at ≈ 5.73 m and a 6.0 m bottom chord is NOT reachable: the halo then trims at ≈ 5.3 m (bottom chord), still 0.3 m clear of the press crown in plan terms (it is not over the press). Measure the rail.
height_check.press: Nothing hangs over the press in plan (x 0.25-3.05, z 0.2-3.2, crown 5.6 m): the nearest steel is the base edge at z ≥ 3.50 and the right base corner's lamp body at z ≥ 3.49.

rigging.hoist: chain hoist 500 kg, BGV-D8+ (e.g. ChainMaster D8Plus 500 kg SK030/76U; CM Lodestar class)
rigging.hoist_source: ChainMaster D8Plus 500 kg data sheet: 'Weight (without chain): approx. 20 kg', chain 0.59 kg/m (P5.4 x 15)
rigging.per_point: Each corner: a two-leg bridle (a V, legs ±0.75 m, 0.75 m deep: 90° between the legs, each leg ≈ 0.71 x the pick) on beam clamps, a chain hoist hook-suspended under its ring, the chain and a round sling round the corner block; a safety steel from the corner to the crane, independent of the hoist. Base corners: the V along the back girder (it holds x). Apex: the V along the outrigger (it holds z). Three V's in two directions hold the halo in x, z and in turn.
rigging.crane: the nave's entry-end bridge crane, rolled along its runway to park over the DJ; rail height 7.6 m (disputed 6.6-8.4), girder bottom 8.15 m, two 0.7 m box girders at ±1.1 m
rigging.signoff: rigging sign-off owed (crane rated load, lock-out, hoists + safety steels): the crane's rated load and a check of the old runway, rails and brakes; the crane locked in place and its power isolated for the whole event; the apex OUTRIGGER is a cantilever off the bridge (its back clamps are pulled up) and needs a structural engineer's check or a different pick (a bridle to the roof steel, or a 3 m halo that fits under the bridge); a rigger's plan with the point loads, signed by a structural or rigging engineer. This file draws it; they approve it.

sway.concern: Owner, 2026-09-29: moving heads may swing a chain-hung truss.
sway.method: A chain-hung load is a pendulum, T = 2π√(L/g), L = pivot to the load's centre of mass. Out of a bridle's plane the pivot is the girder; in its plane the V is triangulated (stiff). The three V's lie in two directions (x at the base, z at the apex), so the halo is held in x, z and turn; the pendulum below is the bound if a bridle is left out.

rule.text: No head moves full range faster than 4 s (every cue that moves a halo head fades ≥ 4 s; a strobe hit moves nothing); no periodic movement (a chase, a sweep FX) with a period between 1.5 and 6 s — half to twice the pendulum's period — on the halo's heads; heads reposition in black.

sway.tie_offs: Not drawn: with the three bridles none is needed on paper. If the rigger wants more, tie the base corners back to the crane girders with horizontal ratchet straps — never to the crowd floor.

halo-apex.note: the apex's beam, hung under the corner block over the pit (x 0, z 7.1)

halo-base.note: the base corners' beams, hung (x ±2, z 3.65), behind the DJ; they make the X

halo-sides.note: two beams on each long side at a third and two thirds from the apex (x ±0.67 z 5.95; x ±1.33 z 4.80), hung

strobe-halo.note: 2 strobes hung under the base edge (x ±0.8), behind the DJ, facing the crowd

par-bridge-back.note: 2 PARs standing on the base edge's top chord, grazing the underside of the BACK girder (over them) outward in deep red

par-bridge-front.note: 2 PARs standing on the sides' top chord (x ±0.6, z 6.07), grazing the underside of the audience-side girder outward in deep red

halo-one-beam.title: Blackout + one beam
halo-one-beam.intent: Everything out but one: the apex beam, hung at the triangle's point over the pit, straight down — a white pillar between the crowd and the DJ, who stands behind it as a shape. The other six halo beams wait in the dark already turned to the next look (a move in black, never a move seen).

halo-slow-sweep.title: Slow sweep
halo-slow-sweep.intent: The halo opens OUTWARD to the crowd: all seven beams leave the triangle along its own directions, bent toward the house and dipped 24° under the horizon, over the heads of the floor; the column beams lean out to the walls in pairs, the columns and the bridge glow low red. A held frame of a slow sweep; nothing flashes.

halo-red-room.title: Red room
halo-red-room.intent: Deep red, and low: the apex and the four side beams stand round the DJ as a red cage landing on the floor 2.6 m out from him; the two base-corner beams cross in an X just over his head (3.1 m above the deck) and run on down past him — the X on the DJ. The columns, the press and the bridge glow red from below; the roof stays black.

halo-white-cathedral.title: White cathedral
halo-white-cathedral.intent: The cone on the DJ: all seven halo beams close in to a ring 1.3 m round the performer at deck height — a cone of cold white with the DJ standing untouched inside it; the column beams stand straight up in mirrored pairs down the nave. Everything else dark.

halo-strobe-hit.title: Strobe hit
halo-strobe-hit.intent: The peak: the two strobes on the halo's base edge flash out over the DJ into the crowd and the pit strobes rake up from the floor; every beam and PAR out so the flash lands on black. The halo beams keep the cone's aim, dark (no head moves under a strobe).

show.why: Minimal's five cues and holds (one 60 s pass), re-aimed for the halo; fades lengthened to ≥ 4 s wherever a halo head moves (sway rule), the strobe hit moves nothing.
